summary: regex_splitter joins the sub-chunk suffix to the label with no separator
description:
`subsplit` in `scripts/chunkers/regex_splitter.py` appends `_letter_suffix(idx)`
directly to `section_label` (line ~206). When the label ends in a digit that
reads fine — `Section 1` -> `Section 1a`. When it ends in a letter the suffix
fuses into the word:

    The Monad              -> The Monada, The Monadb
    Preface                -> Prefacea, Prefaceb
    Chapter I              -> Chapter Ia, Chapter Ib
    Rune XXXVIII           -> Rune XXXVIIIa
    Document FIRST         -> Document FIRSTa
    Tale KILHWCH AND OLWEN -> Tale KILHWCH AND OLWENa

`section` is what a citation renders, so these are reader-facing strings.

## Scope, measured 2026-08-10 over corpus/

- 170 of 239 texts carry split-suffixed labels at all.
- 156 of those suffix a stem ending in a digit/space — reads correctly.
- 19 fuse onto a word ending in a letter: mabinogion, kalevala,
  julian-revelations, iamblichus-on-the-mysteries, pistis-sophia,
  eckhart-sermons-field, dionysius-mystical-theology, dionysius-divine-names-4,
  heroic-enthusiasts-pt1/pt2, masnavi-book-1, secret-teachings-of-all-ages,
  transcendental-magic-doctrine/-ritual, eastman-soul-of-indian,
  plato-phaedo/-phaedrus/-symposium/-timaeus, apocryphon-of-john.

Roman numerals are the worst: `Chapter VIa` is ambiguous between VI + "a" and
V + "ia", and a reader cannot tell a chunker suffix from an authorial
subdivision.

## The fix already exists in the sibling chunker

`scripts/chunkers/page_chunker.py:156` handles the same case correctly:

    sub.section_label = f"{label} (part {i + 1})"

`regex_splitter` should adopt a separator. Whether to match `(part N)` exactly
is the open question: it loses base-26 compactness, and sections here routinely
exceed 26 sub-chunks (iamblichus Chapter VIII 66, pistis-sophia Document FIRST
49, plato-phaedo Section 1 44) — so `part 66` is arguably clearer than `bf`.

## Not a base-26 bug

`_letter_suffix` is bijective base-26 by design (`...z, aa, ab`) and is
correct. `aa` follows `z`; it is not a re-split of an `a` chunk. An earlier fix
(todo:f39248b9) replaced `chr(ord('a') + idx)`, which walked past `z` into
punctuation and shipped labels like `...Symbolism{`. This is the second
reader-facing defect in the same suffix scheme; any change must preserve the
>26 behaviour.

## Migration

Changing the format relabels existing chunks. `section` lives in corpus/*.toml
and nodes.metadata_json, and chunk *ids* are file ordinals rather than labels,
so ids and every staged_tag / staged_edge / edge survive a relabel. Re-chunking
is not required — a label rewrite suffices — but it touches ~170 texts and
should be one deliberate pass, not a side effect of the next ingest. If it were
done by re-chunking instead, docs/ingest/05-chunk-config.md requires re-running
clean_bodies.py afterwards.
